screening_decisions.reason: This is a review article discussing drug interactions in epilepsy therapy, not a controlled clinical trial. No randomization or control groups are described.
This appears to be a case report about a single patient, not a controlled clinical trial with random allocation.

This is a randomized controlled study with 200 patients randomized to two groups (PHT vs no PHT). It is an open-label (unblinded) controlled trial with observation in the control group (no PHT administered).
This is a prospective observational study evaluating risk of postoperative seizures, not a randomized controlled trial.
This is a practice parameter/guideline document from the American Academy of Neurology, not a clinical trial.

This is explicitly stated as a retrospective study, not a randomized controlled trial.

This is a double-blind trial of phenytoin therapy following craniotomy. The abstract mentions 'the group receiving the active drug' implying a control group. Double-blind trials typically involve randomization and placebo control.
This is a randomized controlled trial involving 284 patients with brain metastases, comparing diazepam vs no diazepam (observation control).
This is a single-arm observational study of 150 patients receiving oxcarbazepine, not a randomized controlled trial with a control group.
